outcome: HBV DNA load in mothers and newborns
Hepatitis B markers titer in mothers and newborns (e.g., HBsAg, HBsAb)
cohort: The study included twenty-eight hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive pregnant women and their newborns, divided into an experimental group receiving HBIG and a control group.
finding: The primary finding is that HBIG forms an immune barrier in the placenta between the mother and fetus, depositing in Hofbauer cells and villous capillary endothelial cells, to prevent HBV transmission rather than directly influencing viral replication.
